10.label: Beadle van
10.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

28.label: Beadle Tanner
28.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

68.label: The Ward by Heart
68.desc: Three rounds of the ward, and you notice you no longer look at the doors. You know which are shut and which only look it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Everything in Explore takes a fifth less time.)

72.label: The Old Examiner's Method
72.desc: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Witnesses keep half again as long before they forget.)

91.label: The Fencing-master
91.desc: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Health, for good. With your Health beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: The hard round pays one Coin more: you know where the ground is.)

93.label: False Coin in the Weigh-house
93.desc: The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in the Weigh-house for a year: every coin in the quarter a hair short. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a twist of clippings. (The Market)

100.label: Petition: The Hole
100.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

101.label: Petition: The Apothecary's Key
101.desc: A key to the apothecary's back room and his patience. Needed for ledgers, letters and anything under the glass, and lets you take a token back to the bench once for more. Costs 5 Coin.

102.label: Petition: The Rolls
102.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

103.label: Petition: The Thief-takers' Office
103.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame. Costs 6 Coin.

107.label: Beadle de
107.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

108.label: Apothecary's Boy Tanner
108.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

112.label: An Inked Thumb
112.desc: A thumbprint, perfect, in printer's ink on the white of the doorframe.

113.label: Ned Visscher
113.desc: Ned Visscher, a discharged soldier. Chews cloves against the toothache, constantly. (Accused in: False Coin in the Weigh-house)

119.label: Partial: The Clippings Assayed
119.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

121.label: ★ The Body at the Crane
121.desc: Els Kuiper was found on a warehouse floor at the Harbour, on Sunday, when nobody should have been there. The scene had been tidied: fresh whitewash over something on the floor. What they missed: a foreman's tally. (The Abbey Close) The crier has sung it: the whole city is watching.

123.label: Partial: The Mould Read
123.desc: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

124.label: The Pawnbroker's Page
124.desc: What came through the pawnbroker's door this week, and who brought it.

125.label: The Market
125.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

134.label: The Beggar's Word
134.desc: She stood where everyone passes, and nobody looks at a beggar. She looked at them.

142.label: A Shell on the Sill
142.desc: A cockle-shell, the Compostela kind, on the sill where a hat was set down.

143.label: The Wrong Gang
143.desc: Nobody was on the roll on Sunday, when nobody should have been there. Somebody came in anyway, and knew the doors.

145.label: Sibylla Hobson
145.desc: Sibylla Hobson, a porters' guildmaster. Has had a key to the house for years. (Accused in: The Body at the Crane)

146.label: The Abbey Close
146.desc: The Bishop's precinct: the hospital, the scriptorium, the sanctuary yard. Quiet at night. Too quiet.

148.label: Alibi: Ned Visscher
148.desc: A night in the Hole for drunkenness.

151.label: Partial: What Was Painted Over
151.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Blood, a great deal of it, and a boot-print in it that the lime kept perfectly.

153.label: Petition: Lantern and Cloak
153.desc: A dark lantern with a shutter, a cloak that is nobody's. Opens the Watch whatever your office, and turns a night in a doorway into names and hours written down. Costs 6 Coin.

154.label: Petition: The Informers' Bench
154.desc: A bench by the back door where the city's whisperers wait. A token that points at a front names it at once; the Coquille shows itself. Costs 6 Coin.

155.label: Petition: The Drill Yard
155.desc: Drilling a watchman costs 1 Coin instead of 2, and at the third drill they learn a new trait. Costs 8 Coin.

160.label: Kit Kempe
160.desc: Kit Kempe, a tavern-keeper. Has ink-black fingers; works a printer's press. (Accused in: False Coin in the Weigh-house)

161.label: Witness: Kunz Kramer
161.desc: Kunz Kramer, a boy who sells kindling. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Weigh-house, and has heard there is a reward. (Witness in: False Coin in the Weigh-house)

162.label: Sibylla Imhoff
162.desc: Sibylla Imhoff, a goldsmith's journeyman. Has pledged the same coat at the Lombard's three times this year. (Accused in: False Coin in the Weigh-house)

164.label: Confessor Molenaar
164.desc: A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

166.label: Deposition: Michel Kramer
166.desc: "Their fingers were black, like a printer's." (Protects kin.)

170.label: Letter: Apothecary's Boy
170.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Costs 3 Coin.

172.label: ★ The Drowned Child of the Mill Race
172.desc: The child drowned the night before the fair. Its sister saw something: the older sister hid in the loft. In the loft where she hides, a bribe of sugared almonds. (The Market) The crier has sung it: the whole city is watching. The Council wants it answered within 19 days, and would take it kindly if a certain patrician, of a Council family, were not the name.

174.label: Ursel Weber
174.desc: Ursel Weber, the victim's rival in trade. Wears a pilgrim's cockle-shell on a greasy hat. (Accused in: The Body at the Crane)

data.who: a porter on the late gang

175.label: Witness: Kit Fuller
175.desc: Kit Fuller, a porter on the late gang. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Mercer Warehouse, and is kin to somebody in the case. (Witness in: The Body at the Crane)

176.label: Neeltje Barker
176.desc: Neeltje Barker, a crane-walker. Drives a dray with a lame grey mule. (Accused in: The Body at the Crane)

179.label: Deposition: Pieter Pauw
179.desc: "A shell on the hat, like the pilgrims." (Wants the reward.)

data.who: a market-woman who was paid in it

180.label: Witness: Neeltje de Groot
180.desc: Neeltje de Groot, a market-woman who was paid in it. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Weigh-house, and has heard there is a reward. (Witness in: False Coin in the Weigh-house)

185.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn C0
185.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

187.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn C1
187.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

189.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn C2
189.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

191.label: Band: The Brass Hands
191.desc: Sworn together by Sworn C0, Sworn C1, Sworn C2, who all walked from you. They feed the Vendetta every week. Post the Watch on them in Attend with a watchman; at Bailiff, go in Disguise to build a case against them.

ask.label: A brawl
ask.text: The bear-garden empties into the lane. A watchman at your side, and it is over quickly. Alone, it is on you.

suspects.motive: The nephew was cut out of the will a week ago, loudly, at table.
suspects.alibi: a night in the Hole for drunkenness

suspects.name: Barent Fuller
suspects.motive: The porter was turned off last month and never paid his last wages.

items.label: The Key Tally
items.text: Who has keys, and since when. Someone has crossed a name out.

result.label: The Key-holders
result.text: Four keys. Three are accounted for. The fourth was "lost" a month ago by someone who still comes and goes.

items.label: A Left-Handed Stroke
items.text: Whoever did this stood on the right and worked with their left hand. The angle is plain to anyone who has seen a butcher.

items.label: A Key, Not a Crow
items.text: the stair from the rooms above: no marks, no damage. Whoever came in was expected, or had a key.

items.label: Disturbed Dust
items.text: Something heavy was moved lately. Lately enough to date it.

witnesses: the woman at the casement opposite

suspects.name: Cornelis Pietersz
suspects.motive: The changer buys clippings by weight and asks no questions, and lately has been selling them.

suspects.name: Dirck Sattler
suspects.motive: The soldier learned to cast bullets in Flanders and found a better use for lead.

suspects.name: Wouter Visscher
suspects.motive: The journeyman has the hands for a die and none of the guild's scruples.

items.label: A set of shears
items.text: Locked away like something precious, which it is.

result.label: The Clippings Assayed
result.text: Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

items.label: The Light Scale
items.text: shavings in the sweepings. The Muhtasib tests weights on market day; this one was tested and passed, which means somebody was paid.

items.label: The Carrier's Chit
items.text: A carrier's chit for a place on Friday's wagon to the coast. One way. Someone is planning to leave.

items.label: A Plaster Mould
items.text: Broken in half in a midden.

result.text: Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

suspects.name: Kit Kempe
suspects.motive: The tavern passes more coin in a night than the Mint in a week, and nobody looks at it by candlelight.

suspects.name: Neeltje Barker
suspects.motive: The crane-walker's brother died on a load the victim swore was sound.

suspects.name: Sibylla Hobson
suspects.motive: The victim was gathering the porters against the guild's masters.

suspects.name: Ursel Weber
suspects.motive: Their rivalry had gone to the courts, and then to threats.

items.label: Under the Whitewash
items.text: fresh whitewash over something on the floor. Somebody cleaned up in a hurry.

result.label: What Was Painted Over
result.text: Blood, a great deal of it, and a boot-print in it that the lime kept perfectly.

items.label: Threads Under the Nails

result.label: The Threads Matched
result.text: Wool and tar, from a heavy sea-coat. The victim clawed their killer, hard.

c171.title: The Drowned Child of the Mill Race

vars.detail: the older sister hid in the loft

suspects.name: Hal Webster
suspects.motive: The child saw what the apprentice did at the sluice, and children talk.

suspects.name: Hans Holzschuher
suspects.motive: The child was another mouth, and the mother's jointure went with the child.

suspects.name: Neeltje Webster
suspects.motive: The quarter has always hated her. That is not a reason, and she knows it, and so do you.

items.label: The Witch Mark
items.text: A brown mark on the midwife's arm. Half the women in the quarter have one. The quarter has not looked at half the women.

items.label: A Shell on the Sill
items.text: A cockle-shell, the Compostela kind, on the sill where a hat was set down.

items.label: What the Sister Knows
items.text: the older sister hid in the loft. A frightened child is a witness, if somebody is gentle.

items.label: A bribe of sugared almonds
items.text: Kept hidden by a child who knew it mattered.

journal.title: They Found Each Other
journal.text: Sworn C0, Sworn C1, Sworn C2: every one of them walked away from one of your cases. Now they drink in the same cellar, and call themselves the Brass Hands.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. The Council elects next week. Your patron's seat is contested. The ledger: no case closed; 3 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Door to Door
journal.text: Around the Weigh-house people are frightened, and frightened people talk. You come away with: Witness: Neeltje de Groot. One door stayed shut, and the street talked less for it.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: You sit. You listen. You let the silence do the work. Eventually Pieter Pauw says: "A shell on the hat, like the pilgrims."

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Magdalena Tanner walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Door to Door
journal.text: Around the Mercer Warehouse people are frightened, and frightened people talk. You come away with: Witness: Pieter Pauw; Ursel Weber (accused); Witness: Kit Fuller; Neeltje Barker (accused). One door stayed shut, and the street talked less for it.

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: The Drowned Child of the Mill Race
journal.text: The child drowned the night before the fair. Its sister saw something: the older sister hid in the loft. In the loft where she hides, a bribe of sugared almonds. The Council wants it answered within 19 days, and would take it kindly if a certain patrician, of a Council family, were not the name.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 10
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Apothecary's Boy. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: Michel Kramer keeps begging your pardon for wasting your time. They are not wasting it. "Their fingers were black, like a printer's."

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Cornelis Molenaar takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God.

journal.title: Door to Door
journal.text: Around the Weigh-house people are frightened, and frightened people talk. You come away with: Witness: Michel Kramer; Kit Kempe (accused); Witness: Kunz Kramer; Sibylla Imhoff (accused). One door stayed shut, and the street talked less for it.

journal.title: Promoted: Bailiff
journal.text: The Council gives you the white staff and the key to the Hole's outer door. The sergeants stand when you come in. Some of them mean it. You are now Bailiff. Watch a door and go in Disguise (Explore), and Deputise a watchman with a case (Attend). The Council will send you up to 4 cases at once, and pay 3 a week.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Blood, a great deal of it, and a boot-print in it that the lime kept perfectly. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 9
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: An Alibi
journal.text: You try Ned Visscher's story: a night in the Hole for drunkenness. It will want checking.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Mercer Warehouse. You find: Under the Whitewash, A Shell on the Sill, The Wrong Gang, Threads Under the Nails. The first name in the casebook: Sibylla Hobson. The case takes you to The Abbey Close. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: The Fire: Dirck Sattler
journal.text: The staff is broken, and the fire follows, before the whole city. It takes most of the morning. The crowd is very quiet by the end, and so is the Market for a week after. The underworld learns your name from it.

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door: Give her a Coin
journal.text: The child gets bread. She tells you who came and went, and the clerks get a story about you. (The Crowd and Dread ease; her word on the case)

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door
journal.text: A woman with a child on her hip has been at the Watch-house door since prime. She does not ask for anything. She just stands there, where the Council's clerks can see her, and she has seen everyone who passed. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Bailiff. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Dirck Sattler
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Dirck Sattler is convicted of False Coin in Imhoff's Tavern, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Dirck Sattler
journal.text: Dirck Sattler goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Branded, The Fire. The Council will follow your word, or its custom.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

journal.title: A Long Rest
journal.text: A week of nothing. Long walks outside the walls. Small beer and bread. Your hands stop shaking on the fourth day. On the seventh you want to go back to the Watch-house, which is either a good sign or a very bad one.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. Els Kuiper was found on a warehouse floor at the Harbour, on Sunday, when nobody should have been there. The scene had been tidied: fresh whitewash over something on the floor. What they missed: a foreman's tally.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. A letter under a good seal waits on your desk. It asks nothing outright. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Taken: Dirck Sattler
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: The Rival Exposed
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. The Council reads the file in silence and sends the Harbourmaster's Examiner back to the Customs House. Your name is spoken in the chamber, warmly for once.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Weigh-house. You find: A twist of clippings, A Plaster Mould, The Light Scale, An Inked Thumb. The first name in the casebook: Ned Visscher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Rafe Tanner takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Anneke de Witt takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: You swear the oath in the Council chamber with your hand on the Carolina, and the clerk writes your name under the last Examiner's, which has a line through it. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Dirck Sattler, a discharged soldier. It has to be.

journal.title: Week 7
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Beadle. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You stand in the Market outside the Watch-house for an hour and cannot make yourself go in. Your hands will not stop shaking. You need rest, and soon.

journal.title: A Small Kindness
journal.text: You catch a cutpurse at the corner of the Market. The stallholder presses coin into your hand and will not take it back. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: New Case: False Coin in the Weigh-house
journal.text: The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in the Weigh-house for a year: every coin in the quarter a hair short. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a twist of clippings.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: An Insight: The Fencing-master
journal.text: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: A Weakness Found
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. They will be careful for a week. One more, and you will have them.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Bishop's Invitation: Send your regrets
journal.text: The Council is pleased. The Bishop's chaplain stops greeting you in the street. (The Council's favour)

journal.title: The Bishop's Invitation
journal.text: The Bishop would be glad to see the Examiner at the cathedral on Sunday, in the front pew, where the city can see him too. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Flogging and Banishment: Kunz Pfister
journal.text: Kunz Pfister is whipped at the cart's tail to the Harbour gate and forbidden the city for ten years. The gate shuts. Some of them come back.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: 1 conviction; 1 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Ottilie Kress has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Kunz Pfister
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Kunz Pfister is convicted of Burglary at the van der Meer House, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Kunz Pfister
journal.text: Kunz Pfister goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea, A Family's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Let It Go
journal.text: You take the papers off the wall. You go to the players in the inn-yard. You do not think about the case for three whole hours.

journal.title: Overheard
journal.text: At the conduit you hear someone talking about False Coin in Imhoff's Tavern. They were there. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: An Insight: The Ward by Heart
journal.text: Three rounds of the ward, and you notice you no longer look at the doors. You know which are shut and which only look it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Kunz van der Meer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: Matthes Tucher keeps begging your pardon for wasting your time. They are not wasting it. "They kept asking when the carrier's wagon left." They also mention Cornelis Pietersz.

journal.title: Taken: Kunz Pfister
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Whatever you were working on is gone before you finish. The city does not wait.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Walk on
journal.text: Not your window. You are home before the bell for once. (The round ends early: Weariness lifts)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: Two drunks, a stolen goose and a lost dog. The dog was the most reasonable of them. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Kunz Pfister, the owner's partner in trade. It has to be.

journal.title: Overheard
journal.text: At the conduit you hear someone talking about False Coin in Imhoff's Tavern. They were there. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

journal.title: Cleared: Moll de Witt
journal.text: Moll de Witt has an answer, and it is a good one: a night in the Hole for drunkenness. They are cleared.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Imhoff's Tavern. You find: A Plaster Mould.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Kunz van der Meer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Imhoff's Tavern. You find: A set of shears, The Light Scale, The Carrier's Chit. The first name in the casebook: Dirck Sattler.

journal.title: The Confessor: Leave the seal alone
journal.text: He is grateful, and says so where the Bishop can hear it. (The Bishop's favour)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: You sit. You listen. You let the silence do the work. Eventually the Tiler says: "They opened the gate with their left hand. I marked it because it is the stiff side."

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Long Rest
journal.text: A week of nothing. Long walks outside the walls. Small beer and bread. Your hands stop shaking on the fourth day. On the seventh you want to go back to the Watch-house, which is either a good sign or a very bad one.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in Imhoff's Tavern for a year: shavings in the sweepings. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a set of shears.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Magdalena Tanner walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 2 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Results
journal.text: Four keys. Three are accounted for. The fourth was "lost" a month ago by someone who still comes and goes.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the van der Meer House. You find: The Key Tally, A Left-Handed Stroke, A Key, Not a Crow, Disturbed Dust. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Barent Fuller. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother: Give him the week, and his wage
journal.text: He goes. The others see it. (Standing rises; Dread eases)

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother
journal.text: One of your watchmen asks for the week: his mother is dying in the Warrens and there is nobody else. The round will be short a man. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Magdalena Tanner takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You stand in the Market outside the Watch-house for an hour and cannot make yourself go in. Your hands will not stop shaking. You need rest, and soon.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the van der Meer House. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Moll de Witt. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Letter of Appointment
journal.text: The Council's seal is still warm on the letter that makes you Examiner. The Burgomaster's chamber is up one flight and has a window; yours is under the stair and has a case on it already. Everyone in the Watch-house knows which one you are looking at.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at the van der Meer House
journal.text: No broken glass at Jörg Fuller's. Whoever came in during the dinner hour used the stair from the rooms above, and left with three silver spoons and a ledger. A neighbour reports seeing nothing at all, which is the strange part.
